ov: About 17 species of New World songbirds, known for loudly copying other birds, insects and frogs. The northern mockingbird, the only common one in North America, is grey with white wing patches and common in towns. Other species live in the Caribbean, South America and the Galápagos.
rg: The Americas. The northern mockingbird breeds from south-eastern Canada through the US and Mexico to the Greater Antilles, and was introduced to Hawaii.
df: Insects, spiders, earthworms, berries, fruit and seeds: mostly animal prey in the breeding season and fruit in autumn and winter.
fx: Mockingbirds can recognise individual people who have threatened their nest.
They are known for singing late at night, even past midnight.
